# EOM — Eye On Metadata

EOM is a free, open-source, cross-platform desktop application for reading, exporting, and stripping metadata from files. It runs entirely on the user's machine; no files are uploaded, no account is required, and no data leaves the device.

## Key facts

- Version: 2.0.0 
- License: MIT
- Website: https://abogo-nono.github.io/eom
- Source code: https://github.com/abogo-nono/eom
- Download: https://github.com/abogo-nono/eom/releases/tag/v2.0.0 
- Author: Abogo Lincoln (https://github.com/abogo-nono)
- Platforms: Windows (x86-64), Linux (x86-64, Ubuntu 20.04+), macOS (Apple Silicon, macOS 14+)
- Price: free
- Open source: yes

## What EOM does

EOM reads and displays metadata embedded in files (EXIF, XMP, IPTC, ID3, container metadata), lets users export metadata as JSON, CSV, or plain text, and lets users strip metadata from a file — either selectively (individual tags) or all at once.

## Supported formats

- **Images**: JPEG, PNG, TIFF — reads EXIF, XMP, IPTC
- **Audio**: MP3, FLAC, OGG, WAV, AIFF, M4A, WMA — reads ID3 and other audio tags
- **Video**: MP4, MKV, WebM — reads container and embedded metadata
- **Documents**: PDF — reads document metadata
- **Extended support**: ExifTool integration provides coverage for hundreds of additional formats including RAW camera files (CR2, NEF, ARW, DNG, etc.)

## Privacy model

EOM is designed around a strict privacy guarantee: all processing happens locally on the user's device. There is no network call, no telemetry, no analytics, and no cloud component. The Windows build ships with exiftool.exe bundled so even that dependency is offline-capable out of the box.

## Frequently asked questions

**Does EOM upload my files?**
No. Every operation is performed locally on your device. Nothing is sent to any server.

**Is EOM free?**
Yes. EOM is completely free and open source under the MIT license. There are no subscriptions, premium tiers, or hidden costs.

**What operating systems does EOM support?**
Linux (x86-64, Ubuntu 20.04+), Windows (x86-64), macOS (Apple Silicon, macOS 14+).

**Do I need to install anything else?**
No. EOM ships as a single binary with no installer. The Windows build bundles exiftool.exe. On Linux and macOS you can optionally install ExifTool system-wide for extended format coverage.

**How do I remove GPS location from a photo?**
Open the file in EOM, find the GPS or EXIF section, then click Remove or Strip. You can strip individual tags or all metadata at once and save to a new file or overwrite in place.

**What is ExifTool?**
ExifTool is a widely-used open-source metadata library supporting hundreds of file formats including RAW camera files. EOM can use ExifTool as an optional backend for extended coverage. It is not required for core functionality.

**How is EOM different from online metadata tools?**
Online tools upload your file to a remote server, which means your photos, documents, and the private metadata they contain (GPS coordinates, device serial numbers, author names) are transmitted to a third party. EOM processes everything locally — the file never leaves your computer.

## When to use EOM

- Before sharing a photo publicly, to remove embedded GPS coordinates and device information
- Before sending a document to verify it contains no author or revision history
- To audit a file and understand everything stored in its metadata
- To export metadata records for archiving or cataloging purposes
- To process files in an air-gapped or privacy-sensitive environment where cloud tools are not acceptable

## EOM vs online metadata tools

| Capability                    | Online tools | EOM |
|-------------------------------|:------------:|:---:|
| Processes files locally       | No           | Yes |
| Requires internet             | Yes          | No  |
| Account required              | Yes          | No  |
| Costs money                   | often        | No  |
| Open source                   | rarely       | Yes |
| Works offline                 | No           | Yes |
| File contents stay private    | No           | Yes |
